pitch_detail.notes: The lower half starts at a big clean flake on the left side of the wall; lay it back, then work up and right along cracks, ramps and corners into a long left-facing corner. Finger cracks in this corner hold some loose rock. Step left into a smaller, cleaner corner, then traverse right under a roof to a splitter crack and flakes, ending with a delicate mantle. Only a few short moves reach 5.10a and the rest is easier with good gear. These four pitches are described together, so individual belay spots are not known.

From the broad mid-face ledge, start at the toe of the upper face and aim for the roof with a little pine beneath it; a lengthy right-facing corner continues overhead. Pulling this roof is the crux. Above it, a long hand crack leads to the belay. The grade token is the route's overall rating, since no pitch grade is stated.
Trend up and right to a comfortable ledge that serves as the belay stance. Little detail is available for this short, easier link.
Begins with easy laybacking on loose rock, and the quality improves higher up. A stemming corner follows, with a hard sequence to exit the corner onto a good ledge. Pitch grade is not stated.
Climb a deep chimney toward the summit, placing protection carefully once inside it. Finish with a few pull-ups and a mantle to top out.
